def: A neural network, usually a transformer with billions of parameters, trained on huge amounts of text to predict the next token. Chat assistants are LLMs with extra fine-tuning.
The task an LLM is trained on and runs: given the text so far, give every possible next token a probability. Generation repeats it one token at a time.
The neural network architecture behind modern LLMs (2017): stacked blocks of attention and MLP layers that process all tokens in parallel.
The function $p_i = e^{z_i} / \sum_j e^{z_j}$ that turns raw scores (logits) into probabilities that are positive and add up to 1.
A model after pretraining only. It continues text well but does not reliably follow instructions until it is fine-tuned.
Giving a model the facts it needs in its context, such as retrieved documents or tool results, so its answer rests on real sources rather than on what merely sounds likely.
A number inside a model that training adjusts, such as a weight or a bias. Model size is quoted as a parameter count.
A function that turns how wrong a model's predictions are into a single number to minimise. Language models use cross-entropy on the next token.
The loss $-\ln p$ of the probability a model gave to the correct class or token, averaged over examples. It heavily penalises confident wrong predictions.
An optimisation method that repeatedly moves each parameter a small step against the gradient of the loss: $w \leftarrow w - \eta \, \partial L / \partial w$.
The algorithm that computes the gradient of the loss with respect to every parameter by applying the chain rule backwards from the output, layer by layer.
A unit of text from a model's fixed vocabulary, often a word or a piece of a word, identified by an integer ID.
A tokenizer-training method that starts from characters or bytes and repeatedly merges the most frequent adjacent pair into a new vocabulary entry.
A learned vector of numbers that represents a token or a piece of text, placed so that similar items have nearby vectors.
The cosine of the angle between two vectors, $a \cdot b / (\|a\| \|b\|)$, ranging from $-1$ to $1$. Used to compare embeddings regardless of their length.
The operation where each token computes weights over the other tokens from query-key dot products and takes a weighted sum of their value vectors.
A mask that sets attention scores for future positions to $-\infty$ before softmax, so each token can only attend to itself and earlier tokens.
Running several attention operations in parallel on slices of width $d_h = d/h$, so different heads can learn different patterns, then concatenating and projecting the results.
Adding a sub-layer's input to its output, $x + F(x)$, which keeps a direct path for information and gradients through deep networks.
A divisor applied to logits before softmax. Values below 1 sharpen the next-token distribution; values above 1 flatten it.
Sampling only from the smallest set of tokens whose probabilities add up to at least $p$, after renormalising them.
The exponential of the average negative log-probability a model assigns to the actual tokens. Lower means the model predicts the text better.

Stored key and value vectors for all previous tokens at every layer, reused at each generation step so they are not recomputed. Its size is $2 \cdot L \cdot h_{kv} \cdot d_h$ times bytes per value, per token.
Fluent model output that is false or not supported by the given sources, arising because the model generates probable text rather than verified text.
